To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a population of NMDA receptors with impaired coincidence detection properties causes subregion-specific deficits in synaptic plasticity and behavioral functions.

a hypomorph mutation of GluN1, the obligatory NMDAR subunit, leads to a specific impairment of hippocampal LTP and spatial memory, and that this is due to the expression of a minority of coincidence detection-imparied NMDARs in the DG.

mice expressing a minority of NMDAR hypomorphs in their entire hippocampal formation exhibit specific deficits in synaptic plasticity and learning in the DG, which is accompanied by a specific reduction in the evoked population response.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the functional consequences of a hypomorphic NMDAR mutation in the mouse hippocampal formation, and we have found that the DG is a particularly sensitive subregion for NMDAR-dependent hippocampal functions.
understanding how the NMDA receptors contribute to the formation and maintenance of memory and how their dysfunction leads to the development of memory deficits.
the functional role of NMDAR subunit GluNR1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N598R mutation of the Grin 1 gene causes a specific deficit in the DG of the hippocampi in mice.
the N598R mutant mouse is a valuable model for studying the functional consequences of minor changes in NMDAR physiology in a subregion- and synapse-specific manner.

the N598R mutation causes a specific deficit in the coincidence detector property of the NMDAR in a subset of neurons and that this deficit causes a subregion-specific functional impairment in the hippocampal circuitry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
minor changes in NMDAR physiology in a subregion of the hippocampi can lead to dramatic consequences in synaptic function, and this can lead to cognitive impairments.
the NMDA receptor system, which has been considered a global coincidence detector for synaptic plasticity, can be functionally subdivided into subregions with distinct properties.
minor changes in NMDAR physiology, caused by a hypomorphism of the Glu1(N598R), can cause dramatic consequences at perforant path synapses in the dentate granule cell layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even a small minority of coincidence detection-imperfect NMDARs is sufficient to cause specific deficits in hippocampal function.

the functional properties of the NMDAR system in the DG can be altered by minor genetic changes that do not affect the properties of the N-Methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDA receptor) system in the hippocampus as a whole.
the GluN2 subunits of the NMDAR can compensate for GluN1 hypomorphs, but only to a limited extent, and only when the hypomorphs are present at a minority level.
